decisive_items: A 35-year-old woman presented 11 weeks postpartum with right breast erythema and pain
Anaerobic culture: Positive for Streptococcus agalactiae, susceptible to penicillin
No abscess or focal lesion in the right breast
response.rationale: Postpartum breast erythema/induration with leukocytosis and positive Streptococcus agalactiae culture fits bacterial puerperal mastitis; R1C adds the specific bacterial etiology to the puerperal context, while R6C is broader.

rejected.why: Identifies organism but lacks the clinical syndrome context
No current drug-induced cause; cabergoline was stopped in 2016
Pituitary MRI shows no discrete mass; prolactin elevation is secondary to lactation
Bacterial mastitis but less specific than puerperal bacterial mastitis
Galactorrhea is a symptom, not the primary diagnosis
Hyperprolactinemia is expected postpartum and not the main issue
